title: Styles
bigQuestion: How do our clothes change with the seasons?
summary: Students learn clothes, seasons and shopping words, report what people say with said/told, report questions with asked (if / wh-), and think about clothing waste and fast fashion.

Which season is your favorite? Why?
Do you like clothes with stripes or spots?

grammar.title: Reported speech with say and tell
grammar.rule: When we tell someone what another person said, we use reported speech. We usually move the verb one step back: Simple Present becomes Simple Past, and Present Progressive becomes Past Progressive. Use tell with a person (told me, told us), but use say without a person (said).
grammar.form: subject + said (that) + subject + past verb | subject + told + person + (that) + subject + past verb
examples: "I need new gloves." → Omar said he needed new gloves.
"I'm wearing my warm jacket." → Sara told me she was wearing her warm jacket.
"We like stripes." → They told us that they liked stripes.
"It is too expensive." → Reem said it was too expensive.

items.prompt: "I'm wearing my sneakers." → Fahad said he ___ his sneakers.

items.prompt: Khalid ___ me he was looking for a new tracksuit.

items.explanation: Sara is talking about herself, so I changes to she.

items.prompt: "We aren't going to the mall." → They said they ___ going to the mall.
items.explanation: Aren't moves back to weren't, and we use weren't with they.

grammar.title: Reporting questions with asked
grammar.rule: To report a question, we use asked. For yes/no questions, we add if. For Wh- questions, we keep the question word (what, where, when ...). After asked, use normal sentence order with no do or does, and move the verb one step back.
grammar.form: asked (+ person) + if + subject + past verb | asked (+ person) + wh- word + subject + past verb
examples: "Do you sell tank tops?" → He asked the assistant if they sold tank tops.
"What size do you wear?" → She asked what size I wore.
"Where are the gloves?" → Omar asked where the gloves were.
"Is it expensive?" → Reem asked if it was expensive.

items.prompt: "Is this tracksuit cheap?" → Reem asked ___ the tracksuit was cheap.
items.explanation: This is a yes/no question, so we report it with if.

items.prompt: "Where are the sunglasses?" → Omar asked ___.
items.explanation: In a reported question, the subject comes before the verb: the sunglasses were.

items.prompt: "What size do you wear?" → The assistant asked me what size I ___.
items.explanation: Remove do and move wear back to wore.

items.answer: She asked me if I liked spots.
items.explanation: Use if + subject + past verb. Don't use did in a reported question.

items.explanation: Is moves back to was, after the subject.

items.explanation: Are you wearing becomes I was wearing.

reading.title: Omar's Winter Trip
reading.text:
It was winter, and Omar's family was going camping near AlUla for the weekend. Omar was packing his bag when his mom came into his room.

"Did you pack warm clothes?" she asked. Omar said he was packing everything he needed. He put in his flip-flops, his sunglasses and a tank top. "It's always hot in the desert," he thought.

In the afternoon, the sun was bright, and Omar was happy with his sunglasses. But at night, the desert became very cold. Omar sat by the fire and shook. His little sister Sara laughed. "Mom told us the nights were cold in winter!" she said.

Then Grandpa sat next to Omar. He took a pair of wool gloves out of his big coat pocket. "I always bring extra gloves," he said with a smile. He also gave Omar his old tracksuit. It was baggy, but it was warm.

The next morning, Omar called his friend Fahad. Fahad asked him if he was having fun. Omar told him he was. Then he said he needed a lesson about the seasons!

reading.title: Old Clothes, New Life
reading.text:
Last month, our teacher, Ms. Huda, asked us a question: "How many clothes do you have that you never wear?" I counted at home. I had eleven! Some were too small, and some I just didn't like anymore.

Ms. Huda told us about fast fashion. She said that many shops sold cheap clothes that changed every season. People buy them, wear them a few times and then throw them away. This makes a lot of waste, and making new clothes uses a lot of water and energy.

So our class had a clothes swap. Everyone brought clean clothes that didn't fit them anymore. I brought a striped dress and two pairs of gloves. I took home a jacket with big pockets and a pair of sneakers in my size. They weren't expensive. They were free!

We gave the rest of the clothes to a charity in Riyadh. Now, before I buy something new, I ask myself three questions: Do I really need it? Will I wear it many times? Can I find it second-hand? Try it! It's good for your wallet and for our planet.

reading.title: Three Shops and One Perfect Dress
reading.text:
Thursday, March 12

Dear Diary,

Today Mom and I went to a big mall in Jeddah. I needed a new dress for my cousin's wedding in the spring.

In the first shop, I found a long blue dress with white stripes. I loved it, but it was too expensive. Mom said it cost more than her new phone! The shop assistant was kind. She told me that the same dress was cheaper in another color.

In the second shop, I tried on a green dress with small yellow spots. It was a beautiful color, but it was oversized. The sleeves covered my hands! The assistant asked me what size I wore. I told her I wore a small. She said they didn't have a small in green.

Finally, we found the perfect dress in the third shop. It was long and simple, and it fit me well. It wasn't too slim or too baggy. It was just right. It even had a pocket for my phone!

On the way home, Mom bought me a silver bracelet to wear with it. She said I was a patient shopper today. I told her I was very tired, but very happy!

Nouf

reading.title: Green and White for Our Team
reading.text:
Our school football team has a new tracksuit, and the students chose it!

Last spring, our principal, Mr. Saleh, told us that the old tracksuits were too small and too thin. He said the team needed something new before winter. Winters in Abha are cold, and the boys usually train early in the morning.

So the art club had a design competition. More than forty students sent in drawings. Omar from Grade 6 drew a dark green tracksuit with two white stripes on the arms. He said green was the color of the mountains around Abha. Everyone loved it!

We asked Omar if he was surprised. He told us he was very surprised and very proud.

The new tracksuits arrived last week. They are warm, and they have deep pockets for gloves. The coach asked every player what size he needed, so all the tracksuits fit well. None of them are oversized or too tight.

The tracksuits weren't cheap, but parents and teachers helped to pay for them. The coach said the team was looking great. Now we just need to win some matches!

Come and watch the team play on Thursday at 4 p.m.

reading.title: Grandma's Box of Treasures
reading.text:
Hi Reem,

How are you? How is the weather in Tabuk? Is it cold yet? Here in Riyadh, it's still warm, but the mornings are nicer now that it's fall.

Last weekend, my brother Fahad and I visited Grandma. She opened an old wooden box and showed us her clothes from when she was a girl. It was so interesting!

Grandma told us that she didn't have sneakers when she was young. She said all the children wore simple sandals in summer and winter. Fahad asked her if she had pajamas. She laughed and said she slept in an old cotton dress!

Then she took out a small white handkerchief with blue spots. She said her mother made it by hand. Grandma told us that clothes weren't cheap in those days, so people kept them for many years.

At the bottom of the box, there was a gold bracelet. Grandma said it was a gift from her father. Then she put it on my wrist and told me it was mine now! I was so surprised. I'm going to keep it forever.

Do you have any old family things at your house? Write and tell me!

Love,
Lama

wordWork.title: Categorizing words: nouns, adjectives and verbs
wordWork.rule: A noun is a person, place or thing (gloves, size). An adjective describes a noun (baggy, warm). A verb is an action (buy, wear). Some words can be more than one type: fall can be a season (noun) or an action (verb, past: fell).

items.prompt: Which word is an adjective?
items.explanation: Expensive describes a thing, so it is an adjective.

items.prompt: Which word is a noun?
items.explanation: Sunglasses are a thing, so the word is a noun.

items.prompt: Which word is a verb?
items.explanation: Wear is an action, so it is a verb.

items.prompt: "These gloves are warm." The word warm is a/an ___.
items.explanation: Warm describes the gloves, so it is an adjective.

items.prompt: "We go to Abha in the summer." The word summer is a/an ___.
items.explanation: Summer is the name of a season, so it is a noun.

items.prompt: "These sneakers fit me well." The word fit is a/an ___.
items.explanation: Here fit is what the sneakers do, so it is a verb.

items.prompt: "I almost fell on the wet floor." What type of word is fell?
items.explanation: Fell is the past of the action fall, so it is a verb.

items.explanation: Bought is the past of the action buy, so it is a verb.

writing.prompt: Write an anecdote about a fashion emergency: a time when you or a friend wore the wrong clothes.
writing.hint: When was it? Where were you? What happened? How did you solve it? Use: said, told me, asked if ... and words like baggy, oversized, warm, size.
writing.model: Last winter, my family went to the desert for a picnic. I wore a tank top and flip-flops because it was warm in the afternoon. At night, it was very cold! My cousin asked me if I was OK. I told him I was freezing. He gave me his oversized jacket. It was baggy, but I felt warm. In the end, we laughed about it.

writing.prompt: Report a conversation in a clothes shop.
writing.hint: Use said, told me/us, asked if and asked what. Move the verbs back: like → liked, is → was, are looking → were looking.
writing.model: Yesterday I went to the mall with my brother. He told me he needed new sneakers. The shop assistant asked him what size he wore. He said he wore size 38. Then he asked if they had blue ones. The assistant said they only had black ones, so he bought those.
